votes.evidence: Read bc7090d:src/listing/load.ts loadOpenAiManifest. If format is not mcp-config and manifest.json.mcpServers is not a string, the else-branch reads root mcp.json/.mcp.json, so an inline object is dropped without any error or listing.errors entry. A Codex manifest with a root `interface` gets format 'codex', so the mcp-config branch never handles it. When mcpServers is a string, declaredMcp only rejects empty, scheme, absolute and '..' paths. Any other in-package path, such as ./cfg/servers.json, is read and treated as valid, and nothing checks that it is the root .mcp.json. In src/rules/listing.ts, openAiServers (l.663) takes servers only from o.mcp.json. So with an inline object and no root mcp.json, servers=[] and o.mcp is undefined, and LST-022/023/024 produce nothing (LST-024 l.970 fires only on o.mcp.error). With a root mcp.json present, the inline servers are ignored in favour of a file the portal would not import. No other rule mentions the OpenAI manifest's mcpServers type or path: grep for mcpServers in listing.ts finds only Claude plugin and serverMap uses. The cited page https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/submission-errors states verbatim: "`mcpServers` must be a string path for the root `.mcp.json`", "`mcpServers` must resolve to the root `.mcp.json`", "Set it to `./.mcp.json` or remove the field", and "A root `.mcp.json` is imported only when the plugin-manifest `mcpServers` field is set to `./.mcp.json`". So the portal rejects both an inline object and a non-root path, and the tool passes both silently. I did not run the CLI repro; the code path is unambiguous. A side note on the same page: the fallback to root mcp.json/.mcp.json when mcpServers is absent goes against the warning that root .mcp.json is imported only when mcpServers='./.mcp.json'. Severity: the rejection is documented and detection is deterministic, so a missing check with an error-level rule is justified. Overall impact is medium: false PASS and server checks skipped.

Built bc7090d in a detached worktree (since removed). I made Codex packages from test/fixtures/listing/openai-valid, with interface moved to the root so the manifest is read as format=codex. Each package had two bad servers: a {url:"http://h.test/mcp", headers:{Authorization}} and b {command:"node"}.
(a) Inline object "mcpServers":{a,b} with no mcp.json: `node dist/cli.js --openai-manifest .../.codex-plugin/plugin.json --target chatgpt` gives 0 errors, 0 warnings, 11 rules run, "NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS · PASS". The cause is in src/listing/load.ts loadOpenAiManifest. Only a string mcpServers goes to declaredMcp. Any other value falls through to the root mcp.json/.mcp.json loop, and the inline map is never placed in o.mcp. openAiServers (src/rules/listing.ts:663) reads only o.mcp, so LST-023 (headers, an error), LST-024 (http URL, local server, more than one server with test_cases) and LST-022 all see nothing.
(b) "mcpServers":"./cfg/servers.json": the file is read and its contents are checked (LST-023 error, LST-024 warnings fire). No finding says the path is not the root .mcp.json. The claim that it is "accepted" is correct as far as the path goes. The "PASS" in the original repro only happened because its servers.json content was valid.
(c) Control, "./.mcp.json": behaves the same as (b).
Docs (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/submission-errors) list these as plugin content errors: plugin_mcp_path_wrong_type "`mcpServers` must be a string path for the root `.mcp.json`." and plugin_mcp_path_unsupported "`mcpServers` must resolve to the root `.mcp.json`." So both are documented, deterministic rejections. Under the project principle each new check could be error level. I rate the finding medium overall: case (a) silently skips server checks that otherwise report an error (LST-023) and lets the package PASS, and case (b) only misses the path diagnostic.
Side note: the same page's warning undeclared_mcp_manifest_ignored says a root .mcp.json is imported only when mcpServers is "./.mcp.json". That makes the current fallback, which reads the root .mcp.json when mcpServers is absent, questionable for Codex packages too.
